nodes.n: 10 PM. The garden side of the Malhotra mansion. A borrowed ladder, a sleeping guard, and an eighty-one-year-old woman in a shawl holding a torch.

nodes.t: Second balcony on the left. If you fall, I never met you. If you break anything, I never met you either.
I'm only here as a lookout. I want that on record. Also, Nani-ji, your samosas are incredible.

nodes.n: You climb. The balcony doors are open. She's sitting on the floor in an old Monarchs T-shirt, eyes red, surrounded by wedding catalogues.

nodes.t: How... NANI. Of course. Of course it's Nani.
You shouldn't be here. If anyone sees, he'll trade you tomorrow and he'll never let me leave this house again.

choice.t: "I didn't climb a ladder to talk about trades."
"Come with me. Tonight. We'll figure it out."

nodes.t: Then why did you climb it?

nodes.th: Because I can't stop thinking about a girl with chilli on her lehenga.

nodes.t: And go where? He'd find us by morning. And Sethi would take everything my father has. I can't run. I tried once. I ended up in your auto.

nodes.n: The city disappears. The catalogues, the debts, the date of the final. For a long moment there's only the sound of the sea.

nodes.t: Three hundred crore. My father borrowed it from Sethi Steel to keep the team. The wedding cancels the debt. That's the whole deal.

nodes.n: Footsteps on the stairs. Voices. You flatten yourself against the wall behind the curtain.
It's Kunal, on the landing below, on his phone. He thinks the house is asleep.

nodes.t: Relax, Papa. Once the wedding paperwork is signed, the debt converts to shares. Fifty-one percent. The old man's out by Diwali. The team is ours.
Meera? She'll do what she's told. She always does.

nodes.cliff: It was never about the debt. The Sethis want the whole team. And Meera is the key.
